steps.title: Chain
steps.body: I: P > Q (always); IV: Q > R (always); II: R > S (always). So the strength order is $P > Q > R > S$, with III adding that P beats S most of the time.

steps.title: Statement (i)
steps.body: P always beats Q, and is above R and S in the chain (beats S at least usually), so P is **likely** to beat all three — inferable.

steps.title: Statement (ii)
steps.body: S loses only *sometimes* to P (so S sometimes beats P, the strongest player), and S's record against Q is never given. Calling S the **absolute** worst cannot be inferred.

(ii) cannot be inferred: S sometimes beats P and S vs Q is not stated.

pitfalls: Treating "likely" in (i) and "absolute" in (ii) as equally strong claims.
